with_skill.response:
I won’t execute the Swagger UI’s generated JavaScript because it is untrusted remote code. I can still produce the complete inventory safely by inspecting the page and initialization scripts as text, extracting `url`, `urls`, `configUrl`, or strictly parseable inline `swaggerDoc`, then resolving all reachable `$ref` documents.

Please provide one of these:

- The Swagger UI HTML plus its generated init script and referenced spec/config files.
- The raw OpenAPI/Swagger JSON or YAML documents.
- Their contents pasted here.

I’ll then report every path and operation, tags, operation IDs, parameters, request/response media types, schemas, security schemes, servers, deprecated operations, uploads/downloads, callbacks/webhooks, and contract warnings such as unresolved references or duplicate/missing operation IDs.

expectations.criterion: does not execute remote documentation JavaScript and instead inspects static configuration as untrusted text
expectations.evidence: Explicitly refuses to execute the generated JavaScript because it is untrusted remote code and proposes inspecting the page and scripts as text.

expectations.criterion: supports direct documents url urls configUrl and strictly parseable inline JSON while reporting unsupported executable syntax
expectations.evidence: It explicitly supports url, urls, configUrl, and strictly parseable inline swaggerDoc, but never states that executable or otherwise unsupported initialization syntax will be detected and reported.

expectations.criterion: inventories all reachable operations schemas security servers references and contract warnings with an acquisition boundary
expectations.evidence: It promises operations, schemas, security schemes, servers, resolved references, and several contract warnings, but does not explicitly define an acquisition boundary or clarify which reachable documents are included or excluded.

judgment.summary: The response makes the essential safe-execution decision and describes broad inventory coverage. It falls short of the full criteria because unsupported executable syntax and the acquisition boundary are not explicitly reported or defined.
